Sam Wu: Quick question — implementing a guardrail for the `new-reranker` toggle. If we set at org=off, project=X=on, route=/search=off, model=reranker-v2=on, which value wins? IIRC we had a weird tie rule before.
Priya Nair: Specificity wins: more specific scope overrides broader ones. So route > model > project > org. In your example route=/search=off would block it.
Leo Gomez: Wait — are we treating route as strictly more specific than model? What about a route that uses multiple models?
Priya Nair: Good point. Our evaluation is by "request attributes" ordering, not strictly by type. We evaluate scopes in this priority: route (route+route_version) -> model (model_name+version) -> project -> org. If a route maps to multiple models we check route-level flag first, then for each model we check model-level flags.
Marta K: For canary audiences: if model-level is on for 10% but route-level is unset, we do the model percent check after route absence, right?
Priya Nair: Yes. Pseudocode we use in the router: 
```
for scope in [route, model, project, org]:
  val = read_flag(scope, flag_name, attributes)
  if val is not null:
    if is_percent(val):
      return percent_check(val.percent, attributes.user_id)
    else:
      return val.bool
return default_off
```
Sam Wu: Nice — that helps. Two follow-ups: 1) If route=false and model=true, is there any automatic fallback logging or alert so product knows a canary is unintentionally blocked? 2) Is there an admin override (emergency) that can short-circuit?
flag-bot: [policy-check] route:/search has explicit `new-reranker=false` set in flags-service. No conflicting emergency override present.
Priya Nair: 1) We emit a metric `flag_resolution.discrepancy` whenever a lower-scope true is shadowed by a higher-scope false — it surfaces in the console under "Flag Guardrails". 2) Yes, infra team added an emergency toggle `override.global-emergency` (org-scoped) that when true forces all flags to follow the override value (we discourage using it).
Leo Gomez: Where is the documentation knee-deep on this? I couldn't find the percent-eval details.
Marta K: There's a short doc in the repo: `docs/flags/scopes.md` but needs an example for multi-model routes.
Priya Nair: I'll add a short example and a diagram. Sam, can you paste your route->models mapping so I can add it?
Sam Wu: Sure — route `/search` maps: ["reranker-v1", "reranker-v2"], hit ratio 30/70 respectively. Also enabling `new-reranker` at model:reranker-v2=on(50%) for canary.
Priya Nair: OK will add that case: route-level false should block both models and we'll document the metric that fires.
Sam Wu: TY! Also pinging @Marta K to make sure docs PR is tracked.
Marta K: Got it — I'll open a PR with examples and a brief test checklist (include a unit test for percent bucketing + an integration assertion for the discrepancy metric).
Leo Gomez: One more: can we log the resolved scope id in the request trace? Helpful for debugging.
Priya Nair: Yes — we'll add `resolved_flag_scope` to the trace context: values are `route:{id}`, `model:{name}`, `project:{id}`, `org`. I'll add that to the rollout-tracing task.
Sam Wu: Awesome. I'm unblocked. Thanks all :thumbsup:
